metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art approvals — the dispatcher case at art:87-89 that wraps `python3 runtime/scripts/build_safety.py`. build_safety.py is a fail-closed auditor for two gates: `voice` (armed when metadata.profile/kind/skill == fellows OR voice_policy == persistent-fellow-selected) and `professor_notes` (armed by beats with requires_approval == professor_notes OR act in FEEDBACK/PROFESSOR_BEAR_NOTES, plus fellows B05/B06). Two verbs: --fingerprints prints the subjects with recomputed SHA-256s and exits 0 without touching the file; the default validates the pasted metadata.approvals block against those SHAs and refuses on missing/wrong/stale. Five fields per record: status=approved, reviewer_type=human, reviewed_by non-empty, reviewed_at ISO-8601 with utcoffset, and every subject key equal to the recomputed value. NEVER signs — the pen never leaves the human's hand. All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workstation against three fixture reels at /tmp/claude-501/approvals-demo-*/. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. No paid API, no upload, no network calls. episode.source_sha256 5aa2c4cd9ca4f2862a4e01ba1929d29938f61965b07d462c7e43e6dc6a4c3270.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the dispatcher case. One case branch, no aliases, forwards $@ to build_safety.py.
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is one case in the art file. Three lines: pattern approvals, exec Python on runtime slash scripts slash build underscore safety dot py, forward every argument. There are no aliases; the dispatcher matches only the exact string approvals. Every rule the command enforces lives in that one Python file.

props.title: art:108-110 — one branch, no aliases
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher:
case "$cmd" in
  # ...
  approvals)
    exec python3 "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/build_safety.py" "$@"
    ;;
  # ...
esac

# The wrapper always: (1) resolves ART_HOME from art's own path,
# (2) execs python3 on runtime/scripts/build_safety.py,
# (3) forwards "$@" untouched, so <reel> and --fingerprints fall through.
props.sparkLine: One case. No aliases. Two verbs.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the two verbs. argparse surface + metadata.approvals shape.
beats.narration_text: Two surfaces. Point it at a reel folder. Add dash dash fingerprints, and it prints the subjects a human would need to sign — nothing else. Leave the flag off, and it validates the pasted approvals against those subjects. Either way, the file changes zero. Approvals live in metadata dot approvals in the beat sheet, written by a human editor. The command is the auditor.

props.title: art approvals — the two verbs
props.code:
# runtime/scripts/build_safety.py — argparse surface
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
ap.add_argument('reel', type=Path)
ap.add_argument('--fingerprints', action='store_true',
                help='print subjects for human review; never signs')

# ...and the two-verb main body:
if a.fingerprints:
    print(json.dumps(approval_subjects(a.reel, sheet), indent=2))
else:
    validate_approvals(a.reel, sheet)

# Approvals themselves live in the beat sheet, in one place:
# beat_sheet.json:
#   metadata:
#     approvals:
#       voice:            { ... a human review record ... }
#       professor_notes:  { ... a human review record ... }

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the five-field human review record.
beats.narration_text: Under the hood, an approval record is five fields. Status equals approved. Reviewer type equals human — never AI. Reviewed by, a non-empty string. Reviewed at, a full ISO timestamp with a timezone. And every subject SHA reprinted verbatim from dash dash fingerprints. Miss one, mistype one, forget the timezone — the gate refuses. The refusal is the feature.

props.title: validate_approvals — the five-field record
props.code:
# A legal human review record — five fields, all required.
"voice": {
  "status":        "approved",
  "reviewer_type": "human",       # NEVER 'ai' — this is the signature
  "reviewed_by":   "Bear",
  "reviewed_at":   "2026-09-09T20:00:00+00:00",   # ISO-8601 + tz
  "subject_sha256": "d3486a7ac5d09…04dbd98e04bf4"  # verbatim from --fingerprints
}

# From build_safety.py — the exact fail-close conjunct:
if (record.get('status') != 'approved'
        or record.get('reviewer_type') != 'human'
        or not str(record.get('reviewed_by', '')).strip()
        or not dated                                   # utcoffset must be set
        or any(v is None or record.get(k) != v        # every subject key
               for k, v in expected.items())):
    raise ApprovalError(...)
# Extra gate: NOTES.md must be non-empty when professor_notes is signed:
if name == 'professor_notes' and \
        not (Path(folder) / 'NOTES.md').read_text().strip():
    raise ApprovalError('GATE professor_notes: NOTES.md is empty')
props.sparkLine: Five fields. Human, dated, verbatim — and NOTES.md non-empty.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — approval_subjects recomputes every run; pasted SHAs are the human's, live SHAs are the truth.
beats.narration_text: And here is the subtle part. The command re-computes those SHAs from the beat sheet every run. It never trusts the ones already pasted. If the narration in the reviewed beat changed by one word after the human signed, the recomputed SHA does not match the pasted one — and the gate refuses. Human review does not stick to a beat sheet, it sticks to a beat sheet as it was on the day the human read it.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — same reel, one word added to B05 narration. Gate refuses; recovery is a fresh fingerprint + fresh human record. Verbatim from demo/RUN-LOG.txt sections 4-5.
beats.narration_text: One failure worth showing. A fellows reel, both approvals pasted, both gates green. Then B05 narration gets one extra sentence added — after the human signed. Re-run. The command refuses: gate professor notes, missing pending or stale. Dash dash fingerprints prints the new SHA. The recovery is the same short loop: hand the new subjects to the human, get a fresh dated record, paste it in. The pen still does not leave their hand.

props.title: recovery   (verbatim; one word changed, one gate refuses)
props.code:
# BEFORE — both approvals pasted, both gates green
$ ./art approvals /tmp/claude-501/approvals-demo-fellows
[exit 0]

# ---------------- EDIT (after the human signed) ----------------
# B05.narration_text:
#   "Great pacing. Tighten the fourth beat."
# becomes
#   "Great pacing. Tighten the fourth beat AND cut the sixth."

# AFTER — same reel, same approvals block, one word added
$ ./art approvals /tmp/claude-501/approvals-demo-fellows
[safety] REFUSED: GATE professor_notes: missing, pending or
  stale human approval; inspect build_safety.py <reel>
  --fingerprints
[exit 1]

# RECOVERY — the error itself names the fix
$ ./art approvals /tmp/claude-501/approvals-demo-fellows \
     --fingerprints
{
  "voice":            { "subject_sha256":   "d3486a7ac5d09…04bf4" },
  "professor_notes": {
    "notes_sha256":     "09686350c0147…d77b",
    "narration_sha256": "e133218aca8bd…0ce68"   # ← new
  }
}
# Hand the new subjects to the human. Get a fresh, dated record.
# Paste it in. Re-run. Exit 0.
props.sparkLine: One word changed. Approval stale. Human decides.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — art approvals. A five-field auditor. Two verbs, neither one signs. It reads the beat sheet, decides which gates are armed, computes the subjects live, and either prints them or checks a pasted record against them. It refuses on missing, wrong, or stale. And the refusal is the whole reason the command exists — a fellows reel with a pending signature never ships.

props.segment: Audit a fellows reel's approvals — do NOT sign for me
props.command: From the brutalist.art toolkit root against a real fellows reel of mine: (1) run ./art approvals <reel> --fingerprints and copy the JSON that prints. (2) Paste it into metadata.approvals in the reel's beat_sheet.json as human review records — status: "approved", reviewer_type: "human", a full ISO-8601 reviewed_at with a timezone offset, and every subject SHA reprinted verbatim. (3) Leave reviewed_by empty and hand the sheet back to me — I fill that field in myself. (4) After I return the sheet, re-run ./art approvals <reel> with no flag and tell me the exit code and the last log line. If the gate refuses, tell me which subject SHA does not match and why.
output: step 1 — --fingerprints returns two subject blocks with SHA-256s
step 2 — pasted record fields must be human-authored and dated
step 3 — the follow-up validate returns exit 0 with no output
